title: Largest Product Slice
statement:
Given an integer array nums, return the largest product of any contiguous, non-empty slice.

Values can be negative or zero. The product of every slice fits in a 32-bit signed integer.

examples.why: The whole array: the two negatives cancel. Tracking only the best product so far drops to -1 at the first negative and ends with 4.
The 0 splits the array. On its right, -5 · 2 · -1 = 10. Any slice that crosses the 0 is worth 0.
The slice cannot be empty, so a negative answer is possible. Starting the answer at 0 or 1 is wrong.

constraints: The product of any slice fits in a 32-bit signed integer
hints: With sums, a bad prefix is just dropped. With products, a very negative prefix can become the best one after the next negative number. What should you remember besides the maximum?
For each end position, keep both the largest and the smallest product of a slice ending there. A negative value swaps their roles.
hi(i) = max(x, hi(i−1)·x, lo(i−1)·x) and lo(i) = min(x, hi(i−1)·x, lo(i−1)·x). The answer is the largest hi seen. A zero resets both to 0 automatically.

explain.intuition:
For sums, the best slice ending here is either this value alone or this value plus the best slice ending just before. Products break that: multiplying by a negative turns the smallest product into the largest. So the DP has to carry two numbers per position.

State: hi(i) and lo(i) = the largest and the smallest product of a slice that ends at index i. Recurrence: a slice ending at i is x = nums[i] alone or an extension of a slice ending at i − 1, so both new values are among x, hi(i−1)·x and lo(i−1)·x: take the max for hi and the min for lo. Base: hi(0) = lo(0) = nums[0]. The answer is the best hi(i) over all i. Zeros need no special case: x = 0 makes both 0, and the next value starts fresh through the "x alone" option.
steps: State: hi, lo = largest and smallest product of a slice ending at the current index.
For each next x: compute a = hi·x and b = lo·x from the old values.
Set hi = max(x, a, b), lo = min(x, a, b), and best = max(best, hi).
pitfalls: Tracking only the maximum, like for sums. On [3, -1, 4, -2] that answers 4, because the -3 that becomes 24 was thrown away.
Updating hi first and then using the new hi to compute lo. Both must come from the previous pair.
Starting best at 0 or 1. A single negative value has a negative answer, and 1 is not the product of any slice.

solutions.title: Every start, running product
solutions.idea: Fix a start, extend to the right while multiplying, and keep the best product seen.

solutions.title: Largest and smallest product ending here
solutions.idea: Carry both extremes of the products ending at each index; a negative value swaps them.

followups: Solve it with prefix and suffix products only, resetting at zeros. Why does the best slice always touch one end of a zero-free block?
Return the start and end index of the best slice.
